title: Pierre Andurand on What Europe Needs to Do This Winter - Odd Lots

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Pierre Andurand on What Europe Needs to Do This Winter - Odd Lots.docx

summary: Odd Lots interview (21 Sept 2022) with commodity hedge fund manager Pierre Andurand on Europe's winter energy crisis. Approach: supply-demand balance modelling for gas and oil; argues Europe can manage via LNG, 15% heating cuts and fuel switching, while oil upside risks (Russian losses, SPR end, China reopening) coexist with a broken, illiquid futures market where he cut positions.

completeness_estimate: 0.88 - first reader caught the gas balance numbers, price cap mechanics, SPR and oil supply arithmetic and illiquidity themes; missed secondary mechanisms (weather, revenue denial, historical thermostat analogue, French nuclear recovery, thin-market skew, oil-vs-coal switching)

claims.speaker: Joe Weisenthal
claims.quote: nothing actually provides more molecules
claims.claim: Price caps and subsidies do not add gas or oil supply, so the energy crisis depends on physical shortage and weather, not financial measures.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: once politicians understand that we have to plan for no Russian gas then it is much easier than you know assuming that it will come and then it doesn't
claims.claim: Planning for zero Russian gas (exports to Europe already down 75%) makes the adjustment feasible and avoids the worst case of assuming supply that does not arrive.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: pretty much almost double the the Imports of LNG and that increasing LNG Supply corresponds to about two cells of the Russian losses so far
claims.claim: Europe nearly doubled LNG imports, covering about two thirds of lost Russian gas, and new import capacity is coming, so import capacity is not the constraint.
claims.direction: less upside risk in European gas

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: Europe being you know what you know like one of the wealthiest continents that they'll be able to most of the competitors for for LNG
claims.claim: Europe's wealth lets it outbid other LNG buyers, so the physical shortage is pushed onto poorer importers.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if we assume that Europe could attract about 40 percent of the LNG additions that will already go a long way in solving solving the crisis
claims.claim: If Europe captures about 40% of global LNG additions (a big bump in 2025) it can replace much of the Russian gas, though not all within two years, so a demand response is needed.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: about 50 is coming from residential slash commercial demand that for heating and cooking but mainly Heating about uh 25 is coming from industrial demand twenty percent of Southern power
claims.claim: Gas demand split is about 50% residential/commercial (mostly heating), 25% industrial and 20% power, which shows where cuts can be made.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: so far we've seen a switch of about 35 percent for oil in the industrial demand
claims.claim: High gas relative to oil prices already shifted about 35% of industrial gas demand to oil, so gas demand destruction began before winter.
claims.conditions: gas much more expensive than oil

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we need to bring the key International and Commercial demand down by 15 percent of the response to lowering the thermostat by three degrees from 22 degrees Celsius to 19 degrees Celsius
claims.claim: In Andurand's balance model, a 15% cut in residential/commercial gas via 3 degrees C lower thermostats plus a 5% cut in power demand removes the need for Russian gas.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if if we don't make steps today to lower demand then we will have some issue um some shortage before the end of the winter
claims.claim: Without early demand cuts Europe faces shortage before the end of winter because storage would run out.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the LNG Imports we present 71 of the import capacity of Europe
claims.claim: European LNG import terminals were running at about 71% of capacity with floating units arriving, so terminals are not binding; the constraint is global LNG supply.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: Global Supply of LNG is about 550 BCM so that's billion cubic meters and it's growing for the next few years um at around 15 BCM per year for the next two years
claims.claim: Global LNG supply of about 550 bcm grows only 15 bcm per year for two years and then about 60 bcm a year, so Europe would have to take about 40% of additions and live with cooler temperatures for two years.
claims.direction: gas stays tight for two years

claims.speaker: Tracy Alloway
claims.quote: Russia is exporting less oil and gas but it's selling that oil and gas at higher prices so it's still getting a substantial amount of money from those exports
claims.claim: Higher prices offset lower volumes, so Russian revenue stays high and sanctions need price caps to bite.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: all the consumers have an incentive in playing game and you know bang bang oil cheaper than what they've done you know in the past
claims.claim: A G7 price cap on Russian oil is enforceable because most buyers gain from cheaper oil, though there will be some cheating.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: lower than current prices obviously and and lower than where China and India are buying it
claims.claim: To work the cap must be set below current market prices and below what China and India now pay, so that Russia still sells but earns less without cutting supply.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if you have to replace all the oil exports to Europe and move them to India and China you need a lot more ships
claims.claim: Rerouting Russian oil to Asia needs many more ships, many of them Greek, so shipping capacity limits cap enforcement and cheating.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: some processes you need natural gas as a fixed token you cannot change it right but some of them you can
claims.claim: Some industrial uses (chemicals, glass, petrochemicals) need gas as feedstock and cannot switch, but many can use naphtha or oil, so industrial demand destruction is partial; strategic industries need government support.
claims.indicator: industrial gas feedstock vs fuel use

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: over the next two to three years it will be resolved through more LNG
claims.claim: The gas shortage should be resolved within two to three years through more LNG and lower unnecessary consumption.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: there should be a switch to to Really invest massively into nuclear like around Europe
claims.claim: Europe needs massive investment in nuclear for base-load low-carbon capacity, but plants take years to build; French reactors at 40 years need maintenance.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the warmer temperatures in the summer make it more difficult to cool uh nuclear reactors so that's why some of them have to shut
claims.claim: Hot summers force nuclear reactors cooled by rivers or sea to shut down, reducing power supply in heat waves worldwide.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we have to make sure that the demand meat Supply as well because if demand is above Supply eventually you have shortages
claims.claim: Subsidies and consumer price caps (UK) leave demand above supply and risk shortages and blackouts; prices must reflect scarcity, and France's regulated prices only rose 4% while UK wholesale pass-through doubled.
claims.testable: partly - demand response to capped vs uncapped prices

correction.issue: Overstates the UK point. Andurand said UK prices are already at least double last year's, so some price response exists, and the problem is that more is needed from government awareness campaigns, not that the cap by itself leaves demand far above supply. He also gave France's regulated rise as 4% this year and 15% next year, not only 4%, and described the UK rise as retail prices doubling rather than a 'wholesale pass-through'.
correction.fix: Governments must ensure demand meets supply, otherwise shortages and blackouts follow; France's regulated electricity and gas prices are up only 4% (15% next year), far below wholesale, while UK consumer prices have at least doubled so some price response is already in place, but more demand reduction is needed.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you can't print energy right you can import some of it but you have limits to how much you want to you can import
claims.claim: Energy cannot be printed and imports are limited to what is available globally, so overbidding for a cargo another country needs raises prices and shifts the bill to taxpayers.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: so I think government should do more um to motivate to encourage I mean first to explain why to go on a public awareness campaign
claims.claim: Governments should run public awareness campaigns to cut demand, because price signals alone will not balance a market where supply is falling.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we had the largest SBR release ever um you know basically by 160 million barrels
claims.claim: The US led the largest strategic reserve release ever (about 160 million barrels over six months, around 1 mb/d, plus 0.5 mb/d from others), which more than offset a Russian loss of only about 0.5 mb/d.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the Russian invasion of Ukraine bought a million barrels a day more production more Supply on the market
claims.claim: Net of SPR releases and little Russian loss, the war added about 1 mb/d of supply, helping explain oil falling since summer.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the fact that Market participants were expecting Russian Supply to go down by roughly 2 million barrels a day and we have not seen that yet
claims.claim: Oil fell since the summer because the expected 2 mb/d Russian supply loss did not appear, SPR supply rose and demand and recession fears grew.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the EU embargo has not started yet right so we are starting in uh could in early December and then products in early February
claims.claim: The EU embargo on Russian crude starts early December and on products early February, so actual Russian supply loss is still ahead.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I believe we're gonna lose some Russian Supply I don't know how much but I would say between one and two million barrels a day
claims.claim: Andurand expects to lose 1-2 mb/d of Russian supply, from the embargo, and from Putin's reaction to the price cap.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the spr release will have to stop I mean already I think the pace of the release is going to slow down now
claims.claim: The SPR release is finite and slowing, so a supply source that depressed prices ends.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: there's probably two million barrels a day of demand that can come back once China you know reopens to the world
claims.claim: Chinese reopening could add about 2 mb/d of oil demand after lockdowns curbed consumption.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the only negative event is uh is is a global recession
claims.claim: Event risks (Russia, SPR end, China reopening) are mostly positive for oil, and the main negative is a global recession, so medium-term risks are skewed up while the short term is dominated by recession worry.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: look at my supply and demand balance for the next few years to me it looks bullish right
claims.claim: Despite the market trading as if it wants to go lower day to day, the multi-year supply-demand balance says prices must go higher.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: they're at 11 million barrels a day production they've never had they've never you know managed to to have that level of production for more than a month
claims.claim: There is almost no spare capacity; Saudi Arabia is producing 11 mb/d, a level never sustained for more than a month before, and most OPEC members are at maximum.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: instead of going like one to 1.5 million miles a day I think they will grow around half a million dollars a day over the next couple of years
claims.claim: US shale growth should slow from 1-1.5 mb/d a year to about 0.5 mb/d a year, so supply growth is limited.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: it's a mix of you know the low hanging foot having been taken already
claims.claim: Shale response is weak due to depleted best acreage, supply-chain and fracking-equipment constraints and shareholder pressure for restraint.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the decline rate for Shayla like 80 percent the first year so they need to really keep on drilling
claims.claim: Shale wells decline about 80% in the first year, so producers must keep drilling just to hold output, and cutting drilling quickly reduces production.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the day where we went down ten dollars a barrel from from like 95 to like from 105 to 95 dollars in less than 24 hours and there was no
claims.claim: Oil futures moved $10 in 24 hours on no news, showing the market had become disconnected from information because of illiquidity.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: it went from 1.4 billion Barrels in 2018 to 300 million today
claims.claim: Non-commercial net longs in oil (CFTC data) fell from 1.4 billion barrels in 2018 to 300 million, so there are far fewer speculative longs.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if a market is twice as volatile they're gonna have half of the position in barrels than they used to have and so that leads to a bit of a Snowball Effect
claims.claim: Funds scale positions inversely to volatility, so higher volatility cuts positions and liquidity, creating a snowball of more volatility.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have some hedging that has to go through which is the main the same type of volume than in the past but in the in the market that is a lot less liquid
claims.claim: Fixed hedging flows in a thinner market move prices much more than before.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if nobody is willing to come and think it's it's cheap to buy it nobody has any risk appetite anymore then then the price doesn't mean anything
claims.claim: With no risk appetite from buyers, the oil price stops carrying information and can fall far on no news, which also hurts producers' financing.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we've had like a structural bullish position on energy and that worked well in the first half of the year and then we gave back some gains
claims.claim: Andurand held a structural bullish energy position that worked in H1 2022 and gave back gains in the following months.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I don't understand really what's going on in the market uh you know I might disagree but I don't understand so I don't want to be too stubborn and and I want to to reduce my positions
claims.claim: When the market moves against a thesis for reasons not understood, cut positions to focus on survival rather than stubbornly defending the view.
claims.testable: partly - rule-based cut after adverse moves testable

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I think U.S is probably going to be close to half of the the LNG growth
claims.claim: The US should supply about half of global LNG additions over three to four years, so US gas producers with export access benefit.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: there will still be you know a lot of money in moving cargos until the U.S has export capacity which I think is not before you know 2026 or 2027
claims.claim: Until new US export terminals open (2026-27) energy prices stay high and moving cargoes remains highly profitable.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: quite positive for you know all the natural gas producers that can export
claims.claim: Thematic positioning for the European energy redesign: long US gas producers with export capacity.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: just being long uranium is probably a good trade being long the companies that build nuclear reactors
claims.claim: Energy security should boost uranium, nuclear reactor builders, solar and wind as Europe re-architects supply.
claims.indicator: uranium, nuclear builders, solar and wind

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: this energy security issue will only I think should accelerate the transition because when you deal with nuclear wind or power you're you know you're not giving that money to autocratic regimes
claims.claim: Energy security concerns accelerate decarbonization, because renewables and nuclear avoid funding autocratic suppliers; the problem is that decarbonization was not fast enough.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: in the short term to keep the lights on to make sure we don't have you know social and rest we have to accept that mock code is being used
claims.claim: Coal and oil use must rise for two to three years to keep the lights on while low-carbon capacity is built as fast as possible.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we can deal with 10 or 15 percent less as enough fat in the system someone in consumption but you can't really deal with 50 less
claims.claim: Society can absorb a 10-15% energy cut but not 50% without social unrest and a financial crisis, so the policy target is moderate demand cuts plus new supply.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: early this year I became less bullish on carbon so on carbon prices the euas the carbon Credit in Europe because I think now the mandates will come you know from the top down
claims.claim: Andurand became less bullish on EU carbon allowances because energy security will drive top-down mandates for nuclear and renewables, reducing the role of the carbon price.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I think it will accelerate it I mean because it's an energy security issue right
claims.claim: Nationalization of utilities (such as Uniper) accelerates the shift to renewables and nuclear because governments act on energy security.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: it's generally generally the countries that have the most issues to start with right so it's more like emerging markets that are an important importers of natural gas
claims.claim: In a bidding war for gas, stress falls on poor importers such as Sri Lanka and Pakistan, which become energy poor, a spillover risk for emerging markets.
claims.direction: avoid or short vulnerable EM importers

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: that will be marginally bullish oil but um it will displace Natural Gas um demand so basically you'll have a bit less demand for natural gas
claims.claim: Gas-to-oil switching in the West is marginally bullish for oil but frees gas cargoes for poorer importers, easing the bidding war.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I do suspect the the natural gas prices to stay high generally for the next two years
claims.claim: Natural gas prices should stay high for the next two years, with the first step down if the winter is managed with little Russian gas.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the first step down will be if we can manage this winter properly
claims.claim: Managing winter with low Russian gas removes the psychological fear premium and gives a large price impact lower.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: there's two conflicting forces one is how much oil we will lose from Russia
claims.claim: Key oil uncertainties are the amount of Russian supply lost after the price cap and the state of the global economy.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: much higher interest rates and still high energy Pisces and the worries about the war and and all that you know makes people want to spend less
claims.claim: Sharp central-bank rate hikes plus high energy prices weaken consumer and business demand, creating a demand-side risk to oil prices.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: more aggressive Russia becomes the easier it is to accept some pain on our side
claims.claim: Europe's willingness to bear pain rises with Russian aggression because of a war mindset, so energy demand cuts are politically durable.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: eventually with time possession will go down anyway due to the lack of
claims.claim: Russian production will decline with time because sanctions block equipment, expertise and investment, plus mobilization effects.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: moving the the thermostat down by one degree has an impact of 10 BCM uh for the for Europe so that's uh about five percent or so
claims.claim: The IEA estimates each degree lower thermostat saves about 10 bcm (about 5%) of European gas, so 3 degrees is about 15%.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: consumption as a percentage of income has been going down in general so energy has been relatively abundant and and cheap
claims.claim: Over almost 30 years energy took a falling share of income, so households heated homes more warmly, meaning there is room to cut without much hardship.

claims.speaker: Tracy Alloway
claims.quote: a lot might even depend on the weather
claims.claim: Whether Europe gets through the winter with little Russian gas depends heavily on the weather, because temperature drives heating demand, which is about half of European gas use.
claims.direction: colder winter raises gas demand and prices
claims.testable: yes - heating degree days versus gas demand and price are measurable

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: have to switch into a war Paradigm and once we understand that uh I don't think the steps we have to make are are too difficult
claims.claim: The energy shock requires moving from a mindset of abundance to a war paradigm; once governments accept planning for no Russian gas, the demand-side steps needed are modest and manageable.
claims.conditions: Depends on political acceptance of the new regime.
claims.testable: no - qualitative judgement on policy reaction

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: Russia would not get 100 billion dollars of European money as a result
claims.claim: If Europe closes its gas balance through demand cuts and LNG, Russia loses about $100 billion of European gas revenue, so demand reduction is also a sanctions tool.
claims.indicator: Russian gas export revenue from Europe (about $100 billion)
claims.conditions: Requires the demand cuts of about 15% in heating and 5% in power.
claims.testable: partly - revenue loss is computable from volumes and prices

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we were living with 15 to 16 degrees in the 70s uh you know during the the energy crisis of the 70s
claims.claim: Historical analogues make a 3 degree thermostat cut credible: indoor temperatures of 19 degrees match the mid-1990s average in Europe and the UK, and in the 1970s energy crisis homes were kept at 15 to 16 degrees.
claims.direction: lower gas demand is achievable without hardship
claims.testable: partly - based on historical household temperature surveys

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: it looks like um you know the work mainly at those power prices the work will be done for some of that capacity to come back online
claims.claim: Very high power prices give operators a strong incentive to finish maintenance on the ageing French nuclear fleet, so part of the offline capacity should return, easing the power and gas squeeze.
claims.conditions: Plants near their 40-year design life need repairs, so recovery is partial.
claims.testable: partly - availability versus power price could be tracked

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the volumes are much lower than in the past the open interest has gone down a lot also in terms of uh positions
claims.claim: Oil futures volume and open interest have fallen sharply, so the market is thinner and the same fixed flows move prices more.
claims.indicator: oil futures volume and open interest
claims.direction: larger price swings per unit of flow
claims.testable: yes - exchange volume and open interest series

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: generally it's been down more easily than ever I would say
claims.claim: In the illiquid 2022 oil market, large no-news price moves have been skewed to the downside, because buyers have no risk appetite and a single seller or bidder can push the price down.
claims.indicator: oil price asymmetry in thin markets
claims.direction: price drops on no news more than rises
claims.conditions: Thin liquidity and low speculative length.
claims.testable: partly - skewness of daily moves versus liquidity could be tested

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: generally gas to all these are cheapest actually because now oil is even cheaper than coal
claims.claim: Gas-to-oil switching is the cheapest substitution route because oil is now even cheaper than coal per unit of energy, so switching away from gas supports oil demand rather than coal.
claims.indicator: relative price of gas, oil and coal per unit energy
claims.direction: oil demand marginally up, gas demand down
claims.conditions: Valid while the oil price is below coal on an energy-equivalent basis.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: not only we can avoid shortages but also it will bring prices down significantly
claims.claim: Public awareness campaigns that cut non-essential demand do two things: avoid physical shortages and bring gas prices down significantly, which helps the global economy.
claims.indicator: gas price response to demand reduction
claims.conditions: Needs coordinated action in the importing countries.
claims.testable: partly - price elasticity of the marginal LNG cargo could be estimated

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: that's a study that was made in 2014 basically to look at the impact of winter indoor indoor domestic temperatures on on Health in general
claims.claim: Andurand sizes the thermostat saving from published data: the IEA's estimate of about 10 bcm (5%) per degree and a 2014 study of indoor winter temperatures for the historical baseline.
claims.indicator: IEA thermostat sensitivity, 2014 indoor temperature study
claims.conditions: Linear scaling assumed for three degrees.
claims.testable: partly - the sources are cited but the linear assumption is untested
